summary: Seven teams, seven names, one straggler. PNN asks why the Black Webb Bandits took the longest to pick a name that is three words and a second B.
incidentDescription:
The **Black Webb Bandits** were the final team to submit their name. **Rumors of cold feet circulated, all eight of them.** The word 'chicken' was mentioned, and PNN would like the record to show it was mentioned by other people, *in a tone of enormous enjoyment.*

By then, the other teams had already named themselves after:

- **Fire.**
- **Underwear.**
- **An actual government cover-up.**

The Bandits arrived last, with **a name that is a spider pun wearing a mask.** PNN has opened a file to determine whether this was a failure of nerve or simply *a failure to escape the panther.*
suspectedMotive:
**PNN theory:** the Bandits spent the better part of a week hunting for a name with more than two puns in it, and settled for exactly two ('Webb' and 'Bandits'). It is the kind of math only a spider can do: **eight legs, one idea.**

**Alternative theory:** a spider-themed team cannot announce anything while a panther is on patrol. *Spiders are experts at waiting for something to walk into their plans. They have simply never been timed.*

evidence.label: Exhibit A — A slight scheduling conflict
evidence.description: A panther traps a spider. PNN's reconstruction of why the Black Webb Bandits may have been difficult to locate before their name announcement. The spider's body language says 'I was just about to send that.' The panther's says 'Sure you were.'
evidence.caption: Illustrative PNN reconstruction. Not footage of an actual team incident. Remarkably few exit strategies. No Wi-Fi for submitting forms.

investigatorNote:
Clueso's findings:

- **The chicken connection:** unsupported.
- **The panther theory:** preferred, mostly because the panther is the right color and he has been hoping for an excuse.
- **A caveat:** a reconstruction featuring a panther is not, regrettably, evidence against the Prowling Purrpetrators.
- **Requested:** more facts and fewer obstacles to his conclusion.
disposition:
**Name recovered. Alibi pending.** The Black Webb Bandits are officially on the board; the reason for their late arrival remains under investigation.

*A word of advice: being last is only embarrassing if it becomes a pattern.* **(It becomes a pattern. See PNN-002.)**

purrHiss.note: Last to submit a name. Eight legs, one deadline.

tickerItems.text: Black Webb Bandits finally have a name. The other six teams have had theirs so long it has a nickname.
Black Webb Bandits post a personal best in the 'choosing a name' event: last. Judges note this was also the previous best.
Eight cold feet reported on one team. Podiatrists call it a record and ask everyone to keep their socks on.
Clueso calls the Bandits' name 'a spider pun wearing a mask.' The mask, PNN notes, is also a pun.

incidentTitle: Last to announce. Too early to bribe.
summary: After finishing last in the name reveal, the Black Webb Bandits staged a dramatic comeback: they arrived before bribing had even opened. Their reward is the chance to do it all again. PNN has never seen a team lap the field and still finish behind the starting line.
incidentDescription:
The **Black Webb Bandits** were last to announce their name. Having apparently decided that being late once was quite enough, they left treats and an 'Are you a witch?' flier **before the witches had announced instructions for bribing.** *A bold leap from behind schedule to ahead of permission.* Wanda, Hilda, and Glenda then reminded the teams that every early bribe would receive **a NO.** The Bandits had successfully expedited their return trip.

In a single week, the Bandits have now been last and early, which scientists describe as 'never on time' and the Bandits describe as 'range.' The two policies on file:

- **The witches:** NO.
- **The Bandits (apparently):** 'ask early, ask often, and bring snacks.'

paragraphs: Some teams seem to be eager to find us… a little too eager. 🧙‍♀️
Wait for our instructions before bribing.  We will answer NO to every bribe until the instructions are announced.
If you try to bribe us before then, your penalty is simple: you’ll have to bribe us again once the announcement is made.

Wait for the announcement.
Save your treats.
And whatever you do… don’t anger the witches.

suspectedMotive:
**Leading theory:** the Bandits, stung by the late name reveal, resolved to be early for everything from now on, *including events not yet invented.* The evidence on file:

- **A spider's patience.**
- **A spider's timing.**
- **A spider's complete disregard for the calendar.**

PNN also considers the possibility that the Bandits read 'wait for our instructions' as *'a suggestion with a deadline.'*

evidence.alt: Black Webb Bandits game flier with spiders, webs, a moonlit witch silhouette, and the question: Are you a witch?
evidence.label: Exhibit A — Printed confidence. Premature delivery.
evidence.description: 'Are you a witch?' asks the Black Webb Bandits' flier. A direct question. An elaborate presentation. A regrettable lack of a starting signal. It is the only flier in the neighborhood that arrived before the game was ready to be asked.
evidence.caption: Broomstick Challenge field material. The paperwork was ready. The witches were not. Neither, strictly speaking, was the calendar.

investigatorNote: Clueso was prepared to blame the Prowling Purrpetrators. **Then he read the name on the flier.** The Bandits had helpfully signed their own scheduling incident. *Eight legs, a printed invitation, and still nobody on the brakes.* He has asked whether the pink team could, just once, be responsible for something this easy.
disposition:
The Bandits' record, as it stands:

- **Last** to introduce themselves.
- **Early** to ask the question.
- **Required** to bring treats again.

The witches get another round; the Bandits get another chance to locate the starting line. PNN recommends waiting for the announcement before attempting any further improvements in punctuality.

**Early. Late. Never merely on time.** The Bandits have apparently decided that *punctuality is for people without range.*

purrHiss.note: Bribed the witches before the witches opened.

tickerItems.text: Black Webb Bandits finish last again, this time in the 'being announced' event.
Black Webb Bandits announce a new strategy: 'Early.' The witches announce a new strategy: 'NO.'
Researchers define 'range': last on Monday, early on Wednesday, and out of permission by Thursday.

summary: Two Tightie Whities. Two dogs. A few minutes apart. PNN examines a routine walk that became considerably less routine when somebody asked a follow-up question, and received a very long pause.
incidentDescription:
An anonymous source ([[redacted]]) out walking their dog filed the following report on the **Tightie Whities:**

- **Two members** of the team, **each walking a dog,** heading downhill just a few minutes apart.
- **One member's dog ownership** came as news to the witness.
- **Asked how long they had owned the dog,** the member appeared, in the witness's estimation, to struggle for an answer.

*A simple walk had acquired a surprisingly difficult history section.* PNN notes that 'How long have you had your dog?' is not usually considered an advanced question.

The **Tightie Whities**, a team named for tight, white underwear, have now demonstrated a second signature feature: loose ends. **A tight team. A loose story.** The dogs, for the record, were composed. *They had clearly read the briefing. Their handlers had apparently only skimmed it.*
suspectedMotive:
**Suspected operation:** leave a secret team meeting in staggered departures, or scout a future prank under cover of canine exercise. The plan, as PNN reconstructs it:

- **Separate the departures.**
- **Bring a dog.**
- **Look casual.**

A promising plan, defeated by *the advanced investigative technique of saying hello twice.* The alleged operation had accounted for timing, distance, and canine support. **It had not budgeted for a neighbor with a memory.**

evidence.label: Exhibit A - The walk-by report
evidence.description: An anonymous source reports two separate encounters with Tightie Whities members walking dogs downhill, only minutes apart. The witness had not known that one member owned a dog and describes an uncertain response when asked how long they had owned it.
evidence.caption: Two departures. One witness. Unfortunate scheduling, and one unfortunate follow-up question.

evidence.alt: PNN pencil sketch of two conspicuously casual dog walkers, one trailing toilet paper from his shoe, with annotations: Act natural, Paper trail, and Dog knows the script.
evidence.label: Exhibit B - Operation Loose End
evidence.description: Clueso's sketch desk reconstructs the alleged attempt to look inconspicuous. The dogs have mastered it. Their handlers have requested additional rehearsal time and a better script. The toilet paper was not in the original plan, which is the problem with toilet paper.
evidence.caption: AI-generated comic reconstruction for the Broomstick Challenge. Invented likenesses and toilet-paper detail, not a witnessed scene. Leave no trace. Except the complimentary paper trail.

investigatorNote:
In Clueso's reconstruction, a ribbon of toilet paper trails from one operative's shoe: the Tightie Whities attempting to leave no trace while providing their own paper trail. He has labeled it *Operation Loose End.* The dogs, at least, remembered their roles.

Clueso remains irritated that the Prowling Purrpetrators have supplied neither a confession nor anything this easy to follow. **He wants it on record that a pink operation would have rehearsed the dog.**
disposition:
**Clueso's assessment of the suspected operation:** elaborate departure plan, insufficient rehearsal for casual conversation. The Tightie Whities appear to have prepared for everything except *'Nice dog. How long have you had it?'* PNN recommends a full dress rehearsal of saying hello. Until then:

- **Two walks.**
- **One tight alibi.**
- **A cover story still being house-trained.**

*Fetch is a game. This was not.*

purrHiss.note: Great departure plan. Shaky on how long they have had the dog.

tickerItems.text: Resident walks dog downhill. Neighbors immediately ask how long they have owned the dog.
Tightie Whities seen walking a dog. Dog seen walking Tightie Whities.
Tightie Whities ask that 'How long have you had your dog?' be reclassified as an advanced question. PNN declines.
One dog's honest answer. Dog has a spotless record and a better memory than its walker.

status: Smoldering. No flames located. Tissue paper under review.
incidentTitle: Pyro Posse sets Area 51 Bureau ablaze. Fire department stands down.
summary: The Pyro Posse, a team named for fire, delivered a dumpster fire made entirely of balloons and party tissue. The Area 51 Bureau, a team named for secrets, now has its trash on display. Both teams are, PNN notes, fully inflated.
incidentDescription:
On the night of **October 8, 2026**, the **Pyro Posse** struck. The team reports the following:

- **Two garbage cans** belonging to the Area 51 Bureau camp were crowned with flame-colored balloons and red and yellow tissue paper. PNN has classified the incident as a *Five-Alarm Party Store Run.*
- **A poster** of the Bureau's logo engulfed in flames was unveiled, complete with scorched agents, a smoking saucer, and a cow in mid-abduction who looks like she wants to speak to a manager.

**The cans were not abducted. They were merely accessorized.** For a team that exists to bury the truth, the Bureau has now been outed by its own recycling. *The truth was out there. It was at the curb. It had balloons.*

**No fire department was called.** Had one been consulted, it would have asked what was burning, been told 'balloons,' and *filed the report under 'hot air.'* The Posse chose a team built on cover-ups and delivered the least covert prank available: **bright orange, shiny, and visible from space.**
suspectedMotive:
**Motive on file:** the Pyro Posse, a team built around fire, has discovered that fire is:

- **Difficult to carry.**
- **Legally awkward.**
- **Unavailable at the dollar store.**

Balloons are, however, **100% hot air,** which the Posse already had in abundance. Their official statement promises to "bring them to ash." *Experts note that ash requires something to burn, and the Posse brought only things that pop.*

Meanwhile, PNN theorizes that the Area 51 Bureau's strategy of staying under the radar has been undermined by two garbage cans glowing brighter than a landing strip. **Unidentified Flaming Objects, identified.**

evidence.alt: Two dark wheeled garbage cans on a driveway at night, each topped with orange balloons and red and yellow tissue paper arranged like flames.
evidence.label: Exhibit A - Two bins. Zero fire marshals.
evidence.description: The Pyro Posse's masterwork: two wheeled garbage cans wearing balloon bouquets and tissue-paper flames like a pair of very small, very flammable-looking centerpieces. The result is a dumpster fire in the sense that it is dumpster-adjacent and fire-colored. A real fire would have required matches, a permit, and a significantly different conversation. The balloons did the heavy lifting, which is the only thing balloons have ever been good at: floating while appearing important.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse. Bin there. Done that. Total fire: decorative. Total confidence: stratospheric.

evidence.alt: Illustrated poster of the Area 51 Bureau logo with three alarmed agents, a flying saucer and smoke, all in flames, over the words A Dumpster Fire. Disaster.
evidence.label: Exhibit B - The Bureau, as the Posse sees it
evidence.description: The Pyro Posse's rendering of the Area 51 Bureau logo, in which three agents appear singed and deeply unhappy, a saucer is smoking like it missed its exit, and a banner reads "A Dumpster Fire. Disaster." The Bureau has spent decades perfecting the phrase "nothing to see here." There is now a great deal to see. It is on fire, and it has a font.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; an artistic rendering, not an event that occurred. The Bureau has not yet commented. It is presumably classified, redacted, or both.

investigatorNote:
Clueso admires a well-executed smear campaign, *provided the smear is pink.* He notes, with professional jealousy:

- **The Pyro Posse built a whole fire brand** and sourced the flames from the party aisle.
- **The Area 51 Bureau, experts in concealment,** have been exposed by a trash day.

Clueso also wishes to know why nobody has set the Prowling Purrpetrators on fire, even in balloon form. He would accept a tasteful bouquet. **He has filed this under Unfair.**
disposition:
**PNN assessment:** the Pyro Posse arrived with a bold slogan, a fierce reputation, and a bag of balloons, and left the Bureau's trash looking like *a retirement party for a volcano.*

- **Total damage:** none.
- **Total hot air:** considerable.
- **Area 51 Bureau:** officially designated a **Dumpster Fire,** pending appeal.

PNN reminds the Bureau that Roswell was a long time ago and this is on their driveway. The Bureau's best move is to classify the incident. The Posse's best move is to pack something that actually burns, which PNN strongly advises against, **because fire is not part of the game.** Stick to the balloons, Posse. *Everything else about this prank was already on fire.*

purrHiss.note: A poster and a bouquet of balloons. Brought hot air to a fire theme.

tickerItems.text: Area 51 Bureau signs a new balloon-defense coordinator. Coordinator is a trash can.
Area 51 Bureau rumored to have taken in its trash can at last. Source: a trash can.
Area 51 Bureau says the trash was 'a normal amount of trash.' The trash is 'cleared.' The trash has a badge.
Area 51 Bureau denies being on the field. Footage shows a field. Footage shows a trash can on it.
Balloon stocks soar on Pyro Posse demand. Analysts warn of a hot air bubble.
Scientists measure the exact amount of hot air in a balloon. Result: 'Posse-adjacent.'
Balloons in the neighborhood: too many. Balloons in the Pyro Posse's garage: yes.

status: Hung out to dry. Forensics declined.
incidentTitle: Pyro Posse airs the dirty laundry. Then sets it on fire.
summary: In one night, the Pyro Posse hung scorched underwear on the Tightie Whities, an unidentified clothesline on the Silver Bullets, and cobwebs on a house with a For Sale sign. They then posted the photos before the victims got home, deleted them, and announced that nobody else is playing. Football officials call this a false start. PNN has questions. Mostly about the underwear.
incidentDescription:
On the night of October 9, 2026, two households ([[redacted]] and [[redacted]]) went to football games and came home to a different contact sport. The **Pyro Posse** had been busy. For the Tightie Whities, a team that named itself after underwear and then acted surprised, the Posse selected the most obvious prank in the history of obvious pranks: underwear. On a clothesline. Out front. **Then they lit it.** PNN's legal desk calls this 'asking for it.' PNN's editorial desk calls it the easiest assignment in journalism and has framed the clothesline.

PNN reports the following with a straight face. The garment in question is a pair of white satin bloomers, which are not tight and, following treatment, are no longer white. Strictly speaking, the Posse did not hit the **Tightie Whities** with a tighty-whitey. They hit them with a loose end, which, given the team's history with loose ends (PNN-003), PNN considers a callback. The charring runs down the middle in a pattern PNN's forensic desk calls 'unfortunately suggestive,' and which the Posse's own banner, hanging on the same line, calls **'The Skidmark Synod.'** PNN did not name it. PNN did not need to. *One must wonder if fire was the only thing the Posse applied to these garments.* PNN has not asked and would prefer not to receive the answer in writing.

The Posse's statement on the **Tightie Whities**:

> The Whitie Tighties, a little distracted, have issues a little embarrassing to discuss. Under a little heat it took on apocalyptic levels. They were torched beyond repair thanks to the 🔥 PYRO POSSE 🔥!!
> — **Pyro Posse**, game group

PNN reads the issues as the underwear's. Anything else would be unkind. The Posse also flipped the team's name to 'Whitie Tighties,' which is how you can tell the writer was either in a hurry or near an open flame.

At the **Silver Bullets**, the Posse strung up something else. PNN has studied the photographs for an unreasonable number of hours and can classify the items only as 'laundry-adjacent': a yellow clothesline of charred blue bundles, clothespinned in a tidy row, over a lawn seeded with paper flames and small white fragments of unknown origin. The Bullets were at the football game. They were blitzed at home. The Posse called the play, ran it, and neglected to tell anyone what the play was. The Silver Bullets' home also has a flagpole, per PNN's source. **A flagpole.** The one structure on Earth built to hoist things where the whole neighborhood can salute them. The Posse used the low line instead and left the flagpole **unemployed**. The Posse released no statement about this prank. The objects released none either.

The same night, the Posse also pranked a third household, the **Black Webb Bandits**, and then forgot to mention it. The announcement did not arrive until late on October 10, the following day, possibly because the Posse was worried about announcing the other pranks too soon. The target: a home with a For Sale sign out front. The Posse draped the sign in orange cobweb, scattered orange flags and pumpkin-faced stakes across the lawn, and left. Flags on the play. Several stuck in the grass. Their statement on the Bandits:

> The **Pyro Posse** were torching their way through the neighborhood and found some spiders who got caught in an orange webb of woe, a complete crape paper trap of catastrophe. And had to raise the orange flag of surrender because of the Pyro Posse. ☄️🔥☄️🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 They couldn’t 🧯the power of the Pyro Posse.
> — Pyro Posse, game group

The number of actual flames at this address was **zero**, making it the first torching ever conducted entirely in crepe paper. PNN also got to the 'webb' pun first, in PNN-001, and will accept royalties in the form of silence. *Priced to move. Staged to scare. Showings by appointment. Bring a lint roller.*
suspectedMotive:
**Working theory:** the Pyro Posse believe the Broomstick Challenge is a sprint. By their own count they have pranked three teams (PNN's count is four, because they forgot one, a first in the long history of pranks) and informed the game group:

> It’s like we’re the only ones playing 🤷‍♀️
> — Pyro Posse, game group

Another way to say this is that a team scored in the first quarter and is performing the end-zone dance before the snap. Everyone else is not absent. They are pacing themselves, which is the one thing the Posse is not. By the final-night Halloween party, an October 9 prank will have the shelf life of a jack-o'-lantern on a sunny porch. The Posse has peaked in week one. PNN would like to be the first to say: **bold.**

Their second theory is that a prank is complete when the victim finds out. The Posse upgraded this to 'when everybody finds out, sooner.' Photos of the pranks went to the game group before the pranked households got home, spoiling the surprise for the people it was meant for and delivering it, free of charge, to everybody else. That is a **false start**: five yards, plus the entire play. The photos were deleted quickly. Many people had already seen them, which PNN understands is how photos work. A Posse member explained, of the deleted photos:

> Sometimes I am fast…. Usually when I shouldn’t be.
> — [[redacted]], a Pyro Posse member

PNN has no further questions and is already commissioning the plaque.

How did the Posse know the households would be at the football games? PNN has opened an inquiry. Suspects:

- A schedule.
- A calendar.
- A neighbor with excellent attendance.
- Purrveillance.
- Phone tapping, which PNN raises purely as a joke. No phone was tapped. The only lines involved were clotheslines.

Clueso demands a full audit of the Posse's intelligence budget, which PNN suspects consists of one clipboard and a group chat.

The Posse also arrived too early with two announcements and too late with a third, which in PNN-002 was the Black Webb Bandits' exact specialty. It is, PNN suspects, contagious. **Patient zero wears black and has a webb.** **Penalty report:**

- **False start:** the photos.
- **Delay of game:** the Bandits announcement.
- **Unnecessary roughness:** one pair of bloomers.

evidence.alt: Night view of a front walkway with a clothesline across it hung with scorched dark laundry, a singed white undergarment glowing red at the center, a poster reading The Skidmark Synod at the right, and paper flame cutouts and glow sticks in the grass.
evidence.label: Exhibit A - The Synod convenes
evidence.description: The Tightie Whities' front walk after the Posse's visit: a clothesline of scorched laundry, paper flames on sticks, glow sticks in the grass, and at the center a singed white garment lit from below in a tasteful shade of emergency. At right, a banner reads 'The Skidmark Synod.' It is the only prank in this case file with its own governing body and a name PNN would have fought.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; a vehicle's details are blurred. Total fire: mostly paper. Total laundry: a full load. Spin cycle: skipped. Whites: separated, then burned.

evidence.alt: A white satin pair of high-waisted bloomers with lace trim lying on a concrete patio, singed at the leg openings and streaked down the center with brown and black staining.
evidence.label: Exhibit B - The garment, post-treatment
evidence.description: The principal exhibit: white satin bloomers with lace trim, singed at the leg openings and marked down the center by a long brown-and-black streak. PNN's forensic desk, which is one person holding a flashlight, has classified the garment as neither tight nor white, and the streak as 'a scorch pattern with a regrettable resemblance to something else.' The brown substance has not been tested, labeled, or discussed at dinner. It is the cleanest evidence PNN has ever been afraid to touch.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse. Evidence of a prank, not of anything the Tightie Whities did. Briefs have been filed. These weren't them.

evidence.alt: A Halloween-style poster headed The Meltdown Manifesto, showing a pair of scorched, dripping white briefs framed by ghosts and jack-o'-lanterns, with four lines of verse beneath.
evidence.label: Exhibit C - The Meltdown Manifesto
evidence.description: The Posse's accompanying artwork: a Halloween poster starring a pair of scorched briefs, dripping in a manner that cannot be described politely. Its verse reads: 'We didn't just burn, we completely melted. We're sticky, slimy and totally infested. We smell like something recently dealt. It's not laundry, it's a tragedy felt.' The underwear is the narrator. This is a first for the PNN desk and, PNN hopes, a last.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; stylized artwork, not a photograph of any real event. Verse by the Posse, narrated by underwear. Critics call it 'a tragedy felt.' The underwear has been unavailable for comment since combustion.

evidence.alt: A green front lawn at night with a yellow clothesline strung along a porch rail and fence, hung with clothespinned singed dark blue bundles, paper flame cutouts on sticks in the grass, and small white fragments scattered about.
evidence.label: Exhibit D - Unidentified Laundry Objects
evidence.description: The Silver Bullets' front lawn: a yellow clothesline of clothespinned, charred blue bundles, paper flames in the grass, and scattered white bits of unknown origin. PNN examined the photo at length and concluded the objects are 'laundry-adjacent.' Theories range from singed denim to deflated oven mitts to a very bad weekend. PNN's formal designation is Unidentified Flaming Objects, Part II. The flagpole, per PNN's source, was not consulted and is a little hurt.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse. No statement was issued about this prank. Asked to identify itself, the laundry stayed silent, as laundry does. The clothespins declined to comment on advice of counsel.

evidence.alt: A glossy Halloween poster taped to a dark door reading We Are the Silver Bullets in flaming chrome lettering, with two frightened cartoon figures riding brooms and the tagline Slow, Unsure, and Completely Disoriented.
evidence.label: Exhibit E - A poster for the Bullets
evidence.description: The poster at the Silver Bullets' door: chrome lettering on fire, two broom-riding cartoon figures who look like they have just remembered something terrible, and the tagline 'Slow, Unsure, and Completely Disoriented.' A bullet that is slow, unsure, and completely disoriented is, ballistically, a pebble. The same tagline would also fit a team that pranked three households in one night and forgot to write up one of them.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; cartoon artwork, not a documentary. The Silver Bullets are now on fire in every sense except the literal one, and were sacked at home by laundry.

evidence.alt: A night photo of a blue and white For Sale yard sign on a black post, draped in torn orange cobweb, with a brochure box marked Take One beside it. The agent's contact details and brochure text are blurred.
evidence.label: Exhibit F - The listing, now with cobwebs
evidence.description: The Black Webb Bandits prank: a For Sale sign draped in orange cobweb beside a brochure box that says TAKE ONE. The Posse, who by their own count were taking three, did not read it. Nothing was strung up, nothing burned, and the sign still says For Sale, which makes this the only prank of the night that did not change the property's status. PNN cannot confirm whether the webbing adds curb appeal. Early reviews say 'spooky.' Hot property, no heat.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; the agent's contact details and brochure text are blurred. Location, location, announcement-location. Last to be announced, first to get a listing: the Bandits are consistent. Open house, open season.

evidence.alt: A wide night view of a front lawn scattered with orange flags and pumpkin-faced stakes, with long strands of orange cobweb stretched across the grass, orange streamers hanging in the trees at the right, and orange webbing on the porch rail at the left. A person on the lawn is blurred.
evidence.label: Exhibit G - The lawn, in fairness
evidence.description: In fairness to the Posse, the wide shot shows real effort: orange flags, pumpkin stakes, streamers, and cobweb stretched across the grass like a very ambitious spider. It also shows what the Black Webb Bandits got compared to the Tightie Whities: a craft project instead of a bonfire of underwear. No fire, no poster, no verse. The Posse brought a web and forgot the torch. PNN has seen this brand before. Last time it was called 'balloons.'
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; a person on the lawn is blurred. Flags out, torches nowhere. PNN-004 called. It wants its hot air back.

investigatorNote:
Clueso resents the claim that the Pyro Posse are the only team playing. **The Prowling Purrpetrators are playing.** They are simply not being caught, which Clueso regards as *an advanced technique and a personal insult.*

He also observes that the Posse knew exactly when two households would be away at football games, which suggests either **excellent Purrveillance** or **a calendar.** Clueso has requested the Posse's sources. He would like to compare them to his own, which currently consist of *a dog-walker and a hunch.*

He adds that the pink team is, for the record, doing absolutely nothing incriminating, **which is exactly what a guilty team would do.**
disposition:
**PNN assessment:** four teams hit, three of them in one night, one of them forgotten until the following day. The Pyro Posse have burned laundry, spoiled surprises, deleted the evidence, and announced that nobody else is playing, *a feat of confidence rarely seen outside a fire drill.*

- **Tightie Whities:** officially a laundry matter.
- **Silver Bullets:** officially unidentified.
- **Black Webb Bandits:** officially listed, subject to inspection.

PNN reminds all teams that actual fire is not part of the game, that Rule 5 prohibits damaging property, and that the correct amount of fire for a prank is a paper cutout on a stick. PNN trusts the underwear was the Posse's to burn and that the lawn's only injury was to its pride.

**Final ruling:** the Posse came, they saw, they posted, and then they deleted, in that order, before the victims got home. **They can start a fire. They cannot keep a secret. They cannot keep a count.** Penalties assessed: all of them. *Case smoldering. Laundry not returned.*

purrHiss.note: Three houses in one night. Posted early, deleted late, miscounted.
Out at the game. Blitzed at home by unidentified laundry.
Webbed, listed, and announced last. Again.

status: Paranoia confirmed. Trust no inbox. Illustrated.
incidentTitle: Pyro Posse can start a fire but can't stand the mail.
summary: The first PNN newsletter went out the night of October 10. By morning, the Pyro Posse had called it spam, answered a rebuttal with canned meat, and, losing, asked whether anyone was a witch. The team that sets things on fire can't stand the mail, and its paranoia about it is, by PNN's measure, *outstanding.*
incidentDescription:
The first PNN newsletter hit inboxes the night of **October 10, 2026.** By the morning of October 11, a member of the **Pyro Posse** ([[redacted]]) was in the game group opening with 'Speaking of rule breaking,' *a bold line from the team PNN-005 reminded about Rule 5.*

The incident log:

- **The complaint:** a 'junk mail list' *cannot possibly be allowed.* The newsletter is treated as a **suspect.** *Paranoia level: rising.* Exhibit: a poster. **It needs a seat.**
- **The pink reply:** a newsletter about the challenge is not junk mail. *Calm. Correct. Foreshadowing.*
- **The rebuttal:** 'clearly spam.' They 'don't make the rules.' Attached: **canned meat.** *The meat didn't make the rules either.*
- **The pink reply, part two:** the black market couldn't afford the Posse anyway, this is a free test of fake-news reflexes, and *you're welcome.* One grievance link attached. **Scoreboard: pink 1, comebacks 0.**
- **The smoke bomb:** a sharp turn toward witches. **Paranoia has reached the witch stage.** In the Posse's world, keeping people informed is suspicious, and anyone calm about it *must know something.*

By the Posse's own standard, its unrequested clothesline on three lawns was spam too, *with more fire and less unsubscribe.* PNN had hoped for a rebuttal. **It got a lunch.**

> Unless of course you're a witch...
> — [[redacted]], a Pyro Posse member, game group

**The topic was spam. The topic became witches.**
suspectedMotive:
**Working theory:** the Posse mistook a newsletter for a fire. Both arrive uninvited and leave everyone talking about what got burned. *Only one has an unsubscribe link.*

Suspects:

- **Being read.** *The defense is expected to plead 'felt seen.'*
- **Edition 001's lead story,** which was about the Posse. *PNN does not believe in coincidences.*
- **A can of something,** held at arm's length *like evidence.*

**The Posse can start a fire. It cannot stand to be filed.** It is fine being the news. It is being delivered that hurts.

PNN has charted the Posse's **paranoia level,** in order of escalation:

- **The newsletter:** *mild paranoia.*
- **The mailing list:** *moderate paranoia.*
- **The unsubscribe link:** *elevated paranoia.* **Obviously a trap.**
- **The pink team's calm reply:** **critical paranoia.** *Too calm. Hiding something.*
- **Everyone who is not worried:** **peak paranoia.** *A witch.*

That last step is the pivot. It has three readings: a **smoke bomb,** a **forfeit** (*the recognized way to lose any argument*), or a **deflection** (*the person most eager to ask who the witches are wants the newsletter forgotten*). Clueso has opened a file. It contains one name, [[redacted]], and a pumpkin. *Neither is talking.*

After a clothesline, a cobweb, and a bin of balloons, *everything looks like smoke. Even the inbox.* **A team this paranoid about the mail should not be reading a newsletter about pranks.** *Nobody is forcing them. That is the paranoia talking.*

evidence.alt: A dark, cozy Halloween poster titled Ignoring the Spam: A Pumpkin's Guidance. Five jack-o'-lanterns, four with flames rising from their stems, sit around a round wooden table in a firelit cave of pumpkin-filled shelves. Above them floats a glowing mock inbox with three messages from a pink cartoon cat sender. The central pumpkin, arms folded, says Sigh, another spam email, just delete them. One pumpkin in the foreground reads a book. Pink paw prints drift from the fireplace. The footer reads Some messages just aren't worth the flame.
evidence.label: Exhibit A - A Pumpkin's Guidance
evidence.description: The Posse's illustrated guide to ignoring the newsletter. **Nothing says 'I'm not bothered' like commissioning art.** Its 'just delete them' advice comes from a team with real experience deleting things (PNN-005). The spam, per the poster, is sent by a pink cat offering 'Guaranteed Pranks.' PNN could not have written a better review. One pumpkin is reading. PNN is counting it as a subscriber. **Paranoia, now available in poster form.**
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; stylized artwork. 'Some messages just aren't worth the flame,' says a poster that took a great deal of flame.

evidence.label: Exhibit B - Independent verification
evidence.description: PNN's Independent Verification Desk checked edition 001 against all nine rules. No rule covers newsletters, no personal information was sold or leaked, and every edition has an unsubscribe link. The Desk is neutral, objective, and located six inches from Clueso's chair.
evidence.caption: Independent. Impartial. Issued by PNN, about PNN. PNN stands by it. PNN would.

investigatorNote:
Clueso's findings:

- **Not spam.** Spam is rarely this accurate.
- **Professional respect.** Clueso has spent six cases suspecting one team on no evidence. The Posse suspected a newsletter in under a day. Clueso considers paranoia a profession, and *he has been outworked.* He is considering offering them a desk.
- **The poster names the sender as a pink cat.** *It is the first physical evidence tying the Prowling Purrpetrators to anything, and it is a drawing.* Admissibility pending. The pumpkins were asked for a statement. They are still ignoring him.
- **One click ends the mail.** The Posse chose a complaint, a poster, a GIF, and a pivot instead. Clueso considers it *a close reader.*
- **The pink reply:** he checked the tone. **Calm.** The facts. **Correct.** The link, hoping for a typo. **It worked.** He finds this deeply suspicious. *Nobody is that good at being right.*
disposition:
**PNN assessment:** edition 001 was cleared by PNN's independent desk (Exhibit B). The likelier explanation is that the Posse took it personally. *Teams with thin skin and a thick file often do.*

- **Pyro Posse:** officially spam-sensitive, unofficially *a subscriber with a poster.* Paranoia level: **severe.** Trust level: **the pumpkins.**
- **Prowling Purrpetrators:** under scrutiny for being too calm, too accurate, and too polite. **Charges: excellence.**
- **The pumpkins:** officially on fire, unofficially *still subscribed.*
- **The canned meat:** returned, unopened. *Still not a rebuttal.*

Fire is not part of the game; the pumpkins' flames are illustrative. Grievances about the newsletter may go to the PNN Tip Line, filed under Fan Mail.

**Final ruling:** a newsletter nobody asked for, answered with a meat nobody asked for. *Case closed. Paranoia: confirmed. Witches: not found, PNN checked twice. Unsubscribe link still available. Flame not included.*

purrHiss.note: Gorgeous poster. Wrong inbox. Trusts nobody, least of all a newsletter.
Answered a complaint with a joke, three facts, and a grievance link. The only complaint on file is that it was too good.

tickerItems.text: Neighbor objects to unrequested mail by posting unrequested canned meat. Sources call the irony "well done."
Neighbor checks newsletter for hidden witches. Finds a sunset and a hyperlink.
Pumpkin advises everyone to ignore the newsletter. Is reading it at the time.
Canned meat shares rise after a surprise delivery. Analysts: 'a very specific bump.'

status: Plates full. Doors shut. Final plate count unknown.
incidentTitle: Tightie Whities bring the treats. Nobody brings the door.
summary: On the night of October 13, the Tightie Whities went door to door with plates of treats and a plan. No one was seen taking a plate. Whether anyone did later is unknown, and PNN has opened a separate inquiry. One member was overheard concluding, 'Man, we picked the wrong night.' PNN has never agreed with anyone faster.
incidentDescription:
On the night of **October 13, 2026,** the **Tightie Whities** set out to bribe their way to a witch, one doorstep at a time. A witness ([[redacted]]) reports the team was seen **carrying multiple plates of treats** to **multiple houses.** The results, in order of declining enthusiasm:

- **Door one:** no answer. *The plate remained a plate.*
- **Door two:** no answer. *The plate remained a plate, now with context.*
- **Door three and beyond:** no answer. *PNN stopped counting. The plates did not.*
- **The takers:** **none observed.** *Treats, it turns out, require a hand to take them. Whether a hand ever turned up is the question.*

One member was overheard delivering the night's only review:

> Man, we picked the wrong night.
> — [[redacted]], a Tightie Whities member, on a doorstep

**PNN agrees.** *PNN also agrees with the doors.*

The **Tightie Whities,** a team named for tight, white underwear, spent an evening **left hanging** by a neighborhood. *Briefs, as they say, were exchanged. The doors declined to reply.* A tight schedule met a loose turnout, and **the plates came up short on takers,** at least **while anyone was watching.**
suspectedMotive:
**Working theory:** the team believed bribery follows a simple formula. *Plate plus porch equals witch.* The formula has since been **audited by reality.**

PNN's candidate explanations for the silence, none of them confirmed:

- **Everyone was out.** *A whole neighborhood, simultaneously, with excellent timing.*
- **Everyone was at a party.** *Quite possibly one the Tightie Whities were not invited to.* PNN has no evidence of a party. PNN also has no evidence of an invitation. **A neighborhood this empty is either hiding or celebrating, and neither involves a plate of treats on the porch.**
- **Everyone was in.** *Lights off, curtains drawn, doorbell treated as a rumor.*
- **Everyone had heard about the Tightie Whities** and *recognized a pattern.* **Alibi stock is at a record low. Doorstep stock is lower.**
- **The night itself.** *A wrong night, by the team's own finding. PNN does not argue with a confession.*

**The plan was complete except for the part where somebody answers.** *A bribe is a transaction, and a transaction needs two parties. The Tightie Whities brought the plates, the treats, and the nerve. The neighborhood brought the weather, the calendar, and a very firm 'not tonight.'*

**The open question: did anyone ever take a plate?** PNN has no report of one. PNN also has no report of the plates going home. *Both facts are suspicious.* The leading theories:

- **The Late Taker.** *One brave soul, at the very last house, took pity on a full plate and a sad face.* **Plausible. Unconfirmed. Possibly sprinkled.**
- **The Self-Serve Finish.** *The team ate the evidence.* **A tight team under pressure, a plate in each hand, and a long walk home.** Motive: *dessert.*
- **The Doorstep Drop.** *A plate left on a porch, a doorbell rung, and a sprint.* **A plate on a porch is not a taker, but PNN will accept it as a lead.**
- **The Undeliverable.** *Every plate went home exactly as it left. A clean sweep, in reverse.*

Clueso has assigned an investigator to **the leftovers.** *He has requested the plates be preserved. He has also asked, off the record, whether there is any brownie.*

Clueso has noted, in passing and with some irritation, that **the Prowling Purrpetrators** were not at the scene. *He considers this the real mystery. He is pursuing it.*

evidence.label: Exhibit A - The doorstep report
evidence.description: A witness reports that the Tightie Whities were seen on the night of October 13 carrying multiple plates of treats from house to house, apparently attempting to bribe their way toward the witches. No one was seen answering the door or accepting a plate. One member was overheard saying, 'Man, we picked the wrong night.' The witness did not follow the team all night, so whether any plate was taken after that is unknown. The number of houses and plates is the witness's impression, not a PNN count.
evidence.caption: Plates delivered: none observed. Plates returned: unconfirmed. A perfect record, pending a recount.

evidence.alt: PNN pencil sketch, drawn as if from inside the house looking out through the open front door at night. Three dejected people in Tightie Whities shirts stand on the step, each holding a plate of cookies, brownies, and candy: a bearded man in a backward cap on the left, a woman with a messy updo in the middle, and a man in sunglasses and a tank top on the right. Their underwear waistbands, printed Tightie Whities, show above their pants. A carved pumpkin sits by the step and a quiet, dark street lies behind them.
evidence.label: Exhibit B - The Doorstep Composite
evidence.description: Clueso's sketch desk reconstructs the night's recurring scene from the doorbell's point of view: **three suspects, three full plates, zero takers observed.** Note the **plates held out like offerings,** the **sad eyes,** and the **waistbands announcing the team name** for anyone who somehow missed it. *The pumpkin has seen this before and is not getting involved.* PNN's artist wishes to record that the subjects looked **exactly this defeated,** *in spirit.*
evidence.caption: AI-generated comic reconstruction for the Broomstick Challenge. Invented likenesses, not a witnessed scene or photo of any participant. At the time of drawing, the plates are full. The doorbell is not.

investigatorNote:
Clueso's findings:

- **The plates.** *Multiple.* Full. Carried **at the ready** to door after door. **Nobody was seen taking what the Tightie Whities were selling, and they were selling it for free.**
- **The review.** 'Wrong night' is the most honest sentence a prank team has produced this season. Clueso is considering framing it. *Not the team. The sentence.*
- **The persistence.** *Door after door after door.* Clueso respects persistence. He has, after all, suspected one team for **seven cases** on **no evidence.**
- **The loose end.** *Somebody, somewhere, may have taken a plate.* **PNN has no witness, no receipt, and no crumbs.** Clueso is treating the absence of crumbs as **inconclusive,** and the **presence of a plate** as **a lead.**
- **The guest list.** Clueso has requested it. *If a party exists, the plates should have been delivered there. Better yet, the party should have been informed that there were plates.* **He is checking whether the team received an invite. He suspects the invite went to the wrong house, which would be the night's second wrong turn.**
- **The pink comparison.** *A pink operation would have checked the calendar, found the right night, and been welcomed with open arms and an empty plate.* **Clueso finds this outcome unacceptable and has requested the Prowling Purrpetrators stop being so well received.**
threatLevel: Fully plated. Takers unconfirmed. Moderately underdressed for the occasion.
disposition:
**PNN assessment:** an ambitious bribery campaign, defeated on the record by the one thing no bribe can overcome: *nobody answering.* Whether it was later salvaged is **under investigation.** The Tightie Whities remain officially **undefeated at showing up** and unofficially **unbeaten at not being let in,** *as far as anyone saw.*

- **Tightie Whities:** **plates full, porches empty, schedule tight.** *Recommended next steps: check the calendar. Then check it again.* **Also: state the final plate count.**
- **The doors:** closed, and **the night's most consistent performers.**
- **The treats:** *whereabouts unknown.* **Anyone with information is invited to file it with the PNN Tip Line, under Leftovers.**
- **The witches:** *not found, PNN checked.* **They were not asked what night it was either.**

PNN reminds all teams that treats are meant for the women playing the game, and that a polite 'no' is a complete answer. **No one should be pressed to open a door.** The game is built on cheerful ringing of doorbells, not persistence at them.

**Final ruling:** a team that picked the wrong night. *Case open on one question: where did the plates go? Bribes: unaccepted, as far as PNN can tell. Doors: undefeated. Plates: last seen in hand.*

purrHiss.note: Brought the treats, the plates, and the nerve. Forgot to bring a night when anyone was home. Final plate count: classified.

tickerItems.text: Tightie Whities bring multiple plates of treats to multiple doors. Doors bring multiple plates of nothing.
Overheard on a doorstep: 'Man, we picked the wrong night.' PNN confirms the night. PNN did not pick it.
Tightie Whities go zero for every door on the street. Coach says the night was 'a bit of a stretch.' The plates agree.
Plate futures flat. Brownie shares hold steady. Analysts cannot locate any actual buyers.
Tonight: full plates, light turnout, scattered porch lights. Clueso warns of a front moving in from the doorbell.
Doorstep backed up with three people and a plate each. No one is moving. No one is answering.
Neighborhood unusually quiet on the night of the 13th. A party may be involved. The Tightie Whities were not told.
Tightie Whities declare the night 'a learning experience.' The plates declare it 'a long walk.'
Anyone who took a plate from the Tightie Whities. No questions asked. One question asked. Where did the plates go?
Doors knocked by the Tightie Whities: many. Doors opened: none observed. Plates eaten by the team: pending.
Tightie Whities file updated: 'Bring the treats. Check the calendar. Repeat in the right order.'
'A plate on a porch is a lead. A plate in a mouth is a confession. I will take either.'

status: Cookies eaten. Bomb defused. Spelling in custody.
incidentTitle: Pyro Posse hates junk mail. Mails a screaming glitter bomb.
summary: The Pyro Posse called a free newsletter spam. It then personally delivered a screaming glitter bomb, with cookies, to the pink team's door. The pink team spotted the word 'stratogy,' defused the card, and ate the evidence. A team named for fire has produced a prank with a plan, a fuse, and nothing burning. PNN calls it a dud with excellent delivery.
incidentDescription:
The **Pyro Posse** told the game group it had pranked the **Prowling Purrpetrators,** whom it described as *easily distracted by our sweet treats.* The pink team's own account of the delivery:

- **The cookies:** pumpkin. *Delicious, per the recipient, and the only part of the plan that worked. PNN has confirmed that the Posse owns an oven. The fire department may stand down.*
- **The cards:** more than one, including a **screaming glitter bomb.** *A scream, a sparkle, and a flap. This was not mail. It was an ambush with a flap.*
- **The tell:** a **misspelled 'strategy.'** *A team built around a plan, undone by the first word of it. PNN has filed 'stratogy' as a noun: a plan that failed its own proofreading.*
- **The defusal:** complete. **The bomb never got to scream.** *Screams heard: zero. Glitter released: classified, and probably in a couch somewhere.*
- **The cookies, part two:** eaten. *Evidence consumed in the line of duty, with an appetite the jury found persuasive.*

The Posse closed its report with a parenthetical nobody had asked for:

> I think they hear us loud and clear. (And no they were not disguised as a witches bribe)
> — [[redacted]], a Pyro Posse member, game group

**Nobody had said 'bribe.' Nobody had said 'witch.'** *The Posse supplied both, in parentheses, which PNN considers the punctuation of a team with something to hide.* This is the same team that, in PNN-006, lost an argument about spam and **asked whether anyone was a witch.** *At this point 'witch' is less a question than a verbal tic.*

The Posse's mail policy is now on the record: **spam is an outrage, unless it screams.** *Unsolicited. Glittered. Hand-delivered. No unsubscribe link, though PNN is told the glitter has an extremely long cancellation period.*
suspectedMotive:
**Working theory:** the Posse took the lesson of PNN-006, *'unsolicited mail is an outrage,'* and promoted it to **'unsolicited mail is a strategy.'** *Spelled 'stratogy' in the field.*

PNN's candidate motives, in order of escalation:

- **Revenge, subscription edition.** The Posse cannot unsubscribe PNN from existence, so it **subscribed the pink team to glitter.** *Glitter has no unsubscribe link and, per PNN's cleanup desk, no end date.*
- **Fuse management.** The Posse's own poster promises **Plan. Fuse. Boom.** *PNN can confirm Plan and Fuse. Boom has filed a formal complaint and is seeking representation.* **It is the first Posse case since PNN-004 with no fire in it at all.** *The fire marshal is bored.*
- **The cookie decoy.** The Posse bet the pink team could be distracted by sweets. *The pink team was distracted by sweets the way a bomb squad is distracted by wires:* it ate one, **read the fine print,** and cut the right one.
- **Sound design.** A scream-based prank needs a scream. *The Posse supplied the card. The pink team supplied the silence. The audience supplied nothing.* **A scream nobody heard is just a rumor with glitter on it.**
- **Vocabulary.** The Posse's poster spells **'Purrpetrators'** flawlessly, *three Rs, one tricky P,* and then **misspells 'strategy.'** PNN considers this an efficient use of effort: **get the hard word right, skip the easy one.** *The pink team's name is the harder word. The pink team notices.*

Every Posse poster on file stars a **pink cat.** One of them is captioned **'Our stratogy is literally burning to the ground.'** *The pink team is not on fire. The dictionary, however, took a hit.* **A fire team with a burning strategy and a typo in the first word.** PNN would call it a **flame-out,** *but a flame requires a spark, and PNN is not seeing one.*

The Posse prints the pink team's name in **letters twice the size of its own.** *That is either a threat or a fan club. PNN is flattered on the pink team's behalf.*

evidence.alt: PNN pencil-sketch suspect composite sheet titled PNN Suspect Composite - Case PNN-008. A large panel shows a grinning, scruffy figure in a burnt-orange hooded sweatshirt with flame patches, standing in a night-time porch doorway with a pumpkin on the step. He holds a foil-lined plate of jack-o'-lantern cookies in one hand, a white envelope with a fizzing glitter-bomb card marked BOO! in the other, and a cardboard sign reading Our Stratogy tucked under one arm. A height ruler runs down the left edge. Smaller panels show a front view, a side view, a close-up of the treat plate, the glitter bomb card, the sign, and a smoking flame patch on the sleeve.
evidence.label: Exhibit A - The Doorstep Composite
evidence.description: Clueso's sketch desk has produced a full lineup sheet: **front view, side view, and an itemized list of the evidence on the suspect's person.** *Treat plate. Glitter bomb. Sign. Flame patch, smoking.* The suspect is **hooded, grinning, and holding cookies,** *which PNN counts as a confession, a calling card, and a business plan.* He stands at the angle of a man who has **never been asked a hard question.** *Distinguishing marks: a sleeve patch of flame that is the only thing in the case actually producing smoke, and it is stitched on.* The sign reads **'Our Stratogy,'** *faithfully, typo included.* **PNN's artist was told to correct nothing, on principle.**
evidence.caption: AI-generated comic reconstruction for the Broomstick Challenge. Invented likeness, not a witnessed scene or photo of any participant. Height: tall enough to see the typo. Smirk: unretracted.

evidence.alt: A round plate sealed in crinkled aluminum foil, held out flat. A plain white envelope with faint handwriting rests on top. A red sleeve and dark hair are partly visible at the edge of the frame.
evidence.label: Exhibit B - The plate
evidence.description: The delivery, foil-sealed and topped with an envelope. Contents per the recipient: **pumpkin cookies,** *delish.* **Foil is nature's way of saying 'don't look.'** *The pink team looked.* The cookies lost. The envelope holds a card, and **PNN is not saying which one screams.**
evidence.caption: Supplied game material, cropped to the plate and envelope. Contents: pumpkin cookies. Status: eaten. Cause of death: delicious.

evidence.alt: A purple Halloween card with a spiderweb, tiny stars, and shelves of orange, red, green, and cream pumpkins, half out of a white envelope. One small jack-o'-lantern on the lower shelf grins in a speech bubble that says BOO!
evidence.label: Exhibit C - The pumpkin card
evidence.description: A shelf of pumpkins, a few cobwebs, and one small jack-o'-lantern **yelling BOO!** at the pumpkins on either side. *They are not looking up, which is also how the pink team handled the Posse.* Whether this is the glitter-bomb card or its decoy is **a matter for the lab.** *The lab has been told to open it outdoors.*
evidence.caption: Supplied game material. Screams on file: one, printed. Screams heard: none, audible. The pumpkins on the shelf stayed in character.

evidence.alt: A stylized poster of a pink cartoon cat, singed and sooty, perched in a burning ruined city. A bundle of dynamite is tied to its tail, and another sits in a blast cloud among pipes and flaming pages labeled Phase 1 and Phase 2. Paw prints glow in the smoke. The title reads PLAN. FUSE. BOOM. and the banner below reads SO MUCH FOR THE MASTER PLAN.
evidence.label: Exhibit D - Plan. Fuse. Boom.
evidence.description: The Posse's own poster, which **maps its whole strategy in three words** and **files its post-mortem in seven.** The flying pages are labeled **Phase 1** and **Phase 2.** *There is no Phase 3.* PNN holds the Posse's roadmap, **and the roadmap ends at a cliff.** *A pink cat, a fuse, and a blueprint that is currently on fire.* **PNN has rarely seen a team do its paperwork on both ends of a failure.**
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; stylized artwork. 'So much for the master plan,' it reads, in the Posse's own words. PNN would have waited a day.

evidence.alt: A stylized poster of a weary, sooty pink cartoon cat holding a scorched card marked with a jack-o'-lantern, in front of a burning ruined city. A red book titled Art War rests on the rubble beside a pile of wreckage. The headline reads CAN YOU HEAR US NOW?
evidence.label: Exhibit E - Can you hear us now?
evidence.description: The Posse's follow-up: a weary pink cat, a scorched pumpkin card, and a red book titled, approximately, **Art War.** *The missing words were presumably lost in the blast. So was the chapter on spelling.* The headline asks a question made famous by telephone commercials: can the pink team **hear them now?** *Per the pink team's account, the screams went unheard.* **The Posse said 'loud and clear.' The pink team heard 'clear.'** PNN is holding the volume knob.
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; stylized artwork. Question on the poster: can you hear us now? Answer on file: the cookies, mostly.

evidence.alt: A stylized poster of a sooty pink cartoon cat lounging on top of the words PROWLING PURRPETRATORS in large scratchy pink letters, with burning ruins behind it. A small notebook labeled Business Plan sits at the cat's elbow. The banner below reads OUR STRATOGY IS LITERALLY BURNING TO THE GROUND.
evidence.label: Exhibit F - The tell
evidence.description: The poster that tipped the pink team off. It spells the team's name **perfectly,** *three Rs, one tricky P, in the largest letters on the page.* It then spells **'strategy'** as **'stratogy,'** *in the smallest.* **The Posse can spell 'Purrpetrators' but not 'strategy,'** *which PNN finds the most backhanded compliment ever printed.* The business plan under the cat's elbow looks fine. **It is the only one in the building that does.**
evidence.caption: Supplied game material from the Pyro Posse; stylized artwork. Strategy: burning. Spelling: also burning. The pink team is fine, thank you.

investigatorNote:
Clueso's findings:

- **The doorstep.** Seven cases chasing the pink team, and Clueso has not yet reached its porch. The Posse got there in one night with **a plate of cookies and a fuse.** *He has requested the recipe. For the file.*
- **The defusal.** The pink team identified, defused, and **survived** a glitter bomb with no training PNN can find. *In Clueso's experience, that is called having done this before.* He has written the word **'yet'** in the margin. **Guilty until proven guilty. Now also proven handy.**
- **The spelling.** Clueso has opened a new crime category for **'stratogy.'** *Penalty: one dictionary, one sticky note.* He is quietly pleased that he can spell **'strategy,'** *since the pink team's file depends on it.*
- **The denial.** An unprompted denial is, in Clueso's view, **a confession in a trench coat.** *He notes that the trench coat was also unprompted, and has glitter on it.*
- **The cookies.** He has requested a sample. **For evidence.** *Probably.*
- **The scream.** He asked for the audio and was told the bomb had been defused. He then asked for **the defused scream.** *A committee has been formed. It meets Tuesdays. It has not met.*
disposition:
**PNN assessment:** a prank with a plan, a fuse, and a typo. **The plan landed. The fuse was lit. The boom filed a late request and was denied.** *The Posse says it hit the pink team. The pink team says the bomb never got to scream. PNN leans toward the version with a defusal, and away from the one with a poster.*

- **Pyro Posse:** **a fire team that finally delivered a prank with no fire,** *all sparkle and no bang, as the fire marshal noted with some boredom.* Delivery: **excellent.** Spelling: **in custody.** Spam policy: **temporarily suspended.**
- **Prowling Purrpetrators:** pranked, unbothered, and spelling-literate. **Charges: situational awareness.** *Under scrutiny for catching a trap on the one word it misspelled, defusing it, and then finishing the cookies.*
- **The cookies:** consumed. *Evidence destroyed by the prosecution, with enthusiasm, in the case's only unanimous verdict.*
- **The glitter:** *still at large.* PNN's cleanup desk expects recovery in **three to five business years,** with sightings reported in couch cushions. **Glitter is the only thing that outlives a grudge.**

PNN reminds all teams that a screaming card is best opened in daylight by a consenting adult. *Never near a child, and never near a nap (rules 6 and 7).* Proof of any prank belongs in the game group by October 22.

**Final ruling:** a Posse that called mail spam, mailed a scream, and denied a bribe nobody mentioned. *Case closed. Boom: declined. Cookies: delish. Witch bribe: officially denied, unofficially noted in parentheses. Unsubscribe link: still available, still unread by anyone with a poster.*
